tables.description: Average monthly returns of winner, loser, and W-L portfolios for the JT, MG, and 52-week high (6,6) strategies, July 1963 - December 2001, all months, equally weighted.
tables.replication_meaning: Proves correct universe construction (all CRSP stocks 1963-2001), correct construction of all three ranking signals (JT cumulative 6-month return, MG value-weighted 20-industry return, 52-week-high price ratio), EW 30/30 portfolio formation, and the overlapping six-portfolio (6,6) holding-period averaging.
tables.paper_quote: This table reports the average monthly portfolio returns from July 1963 through December 2001 for three different momentum investing strategies. ... The sample includes all stocks on CRSP; $t$-statistics are in parentheses. (L81)

tables.description: Same three (6,6) strategies as Table I split into non-January months (Panel A) and January only (Panel B).
tables.replication_meaning: Proves the monthly return series is correctly date-aligned at the calendar-month level: the January-effect decomposition (tax-loss-selling rebound in losers) is a sharp, nonlinear function of the monthly return data, so matching both panels validates the time alignment and the loser-portfolio composition that Table I averages over.
tables.paper_quote: This table reports the average monthly portfolio returns from July 1963 through December 2001, excluding Januaries (Panel A) or Januaries only (Panel B), for three different momentum investing strategies. (L150)

tables.description: Pairwise nested comparison: 52-week-high W-L returns within JT winner/middle/loser groups (Panel A) and JT W-L returns within 52-week-high groups (Panel B), all months and excluding January.
tables.replication_meaning: Proves the independent double-sort mechanics: two signals applied sequentially with 30/30 cutoffs, equally weighted nested portfolios, and the nonempty-cell rule for W-L averages. Since Panels A and B share cells by construction, internal consistency (e.g. the shared winner-winner cell 1.63%) is itself a check on cell assignment.
tables.paper_quote: Panel A reports the average monthly returns from July 1963 through December 2001 for equally weighted portfolios that are long 52-week winners and short 52-week losers within winner, middle, and loser categories identified by JT's strategy. Panel B reports returns for equally weighted portfolios formed using JT's strategy within groups identified as winner, middle, and loser by the 52-week high strategy. (L251)

tables.description: Fama-MacBeth cross-sectional regressions with strategy dummy variables (JT, MG, 52-week high), controls R_{i,t-1} and size, one-month skip; (6,6) and (6,12) strategies, raw and Fama-French risk-adjusted returns, January included and excluded.
tables.replication_meaning: Proves the Fama-MacBeth dummy-variable regression design: month-by-month cross-sectional regressions for each formation lag j=2..7 (6,6) and j=2..13 (6,12) with the one-month skip, correct dummy construction from all three rankings at t-j, size and lagged-return controls, coefficient averaging across j, time-series averaging with t-stats from the time series, and the FF (1996) risk-adjustment intercepts.
tables.paper_quote: Each month between July 1963 and December 2001, 6 ($j = 2, \ldots, 7$) or 12 ($j = 2, \ldots, 13$) cross-sectional regressions of the following form are estimated for (6, 6) and (6, 12) strategies, respectively ... The numbers reported for the raw return in the tables are the time-series averages of these averages. They are in percent per month. (L625, L631)

tables.description: Table V extended with Grinblatt-Han (2002) embedded-capital-gain winner/loser dummies; same (6,6)/(6,12) raw and risk-adjusted layout.
tables.replication_meaning: Proves the GH embedded capital gain construction: 60-month turnover-weighted reference price from monthly volume and shares outstanding (V_t = volume/shares), g_t = (P_t - R_t)/P_t, top/bottom-30% GH dummies included alongside the other six dummies, and that the 52-week-high strategy still dominates GH after controlling for the disposition effect.
tables.paper_quote: Table VII is identical to Table V, except that the GH winner and loser dummies are added as explanatory variables. (L1327)

tables.description: Persistence of profits from JT, MG, and 52-week high strategies - risk-adjusted returns, (6,k,12) strategies k=12,24,36,48.
tables.replication_meaning: Tests the paper's 3rd abstract claim: JT/MG momentum reverses at long horizons while 52-week-high profits do not.
tables.paper_quote: Table VI presents regression results for risk-adjusted returns... (L985)

tables.description: Table V with a 52-week-LOW strategy (wh_lo_sig) replacing the 52-week high; (6,6) and (6,12), raw and risk-adjusted.
tables.replication_meaning: Robustness/cross-sectional corollary: the 52-week-low spread is insignificant while JT spreads grow, arguing against the symmetric GH proposition.
tables.paper_quote: Table IX is identical to Table V except that a strategy based on the 52-week low is used instead of the 52-week high. (L2176)
tables.notes: size s612_raw_janincl t-stat OCR '(3.68)' corrected to -3.68 (dropped minus; coef -0.17, Table V analog -4.27).
